reasoning: By Mantel's theorem (the r=2 case of Turán's theorem), a triangle-free simple graph on n vertices has at most floor(n^2/4) edges. For n=13, floor(169/4)=42. Proof sketch: for any edge uv in a triangle-free graph, N(u) and N(v) are disjoint so deg(u)+deg(v) <= n; summing over edges gives sum of deg^2 <= n·m, and by Cauchy-Schwarz (2m)^2/n <= sum deg^2 <= n·m, so m <= n^2/4. Construction achieving 42: the complete bipartite graph K_{6,7} with parts A={1,...,6} and B={7,...,13}, every vertex of A joined to every vertex of B. It has 6·7=42 edges and is bipartite, hence contains no odd cycle and in particular no triangle.
